newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Phone accounting rates need reform, official says.
newsitem.headline: Phone accounting rates need reform, official says.

text.p: Urgent reform of the global telephone accounting rate system is vital as free competition in the industry becomes a reality, a senior industry oficial said on Friday.

Tim Kelly, head of operations analysis, strategic planning at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the world's phone regulator, said the system needed reform "because it needs to be adapted to a competitive market environment".
"Accounting rates work well in an environment in which there is one carrier per nation," he told delegates to the Asia Telecom 97 trade fair.
"But as we move towards multi-carrier environments, then the accounting rates system needs to be seriously reformed."

Accounting rates are used to decide how much telephone companies pay each other for international calls. They were designed to compensate phone companies in recipient countries for the cost of completing calls.
But the system was designed when most calls were made between monopoly telecommunications companies and have been criticised for being cumbersome and out of date.

The United States is pressing for a sharp cut in accounting rates because more calls originate from the country than terminate there, leaving U.S. telephone carriers with a bill of several billion dollars a year.
Kelly said a World Trade Organisation (WTO) agreement in February to promote liberalised telecommunications was "the biggest single requirement that has been placed for accounting rate reform".
The accounting rate system, which accumulates three separate charges for international transmission, international gateway and call termination, was now an anachronism, he said.
"One logical consequence of the WTO agreement for competitive telecommunications is that we can begin to view telecommunications as two quite separate markets," Kelly said.
"The first for originating calls and the second for terminating calls," he said.
But the two telecommunications markets that would emerge might see considerable imbalance between levels of competition, he said.
"In the case of call origination, there will be instant competition from day one," Kelly said.
"However, for call termination the competition will pick up much more slowly as the network will evolve up very slowly.
"In most developing countries the new market of call termination would be handled by incumbent ex-monopolies where there would be clear roles for the regulator to play," Kelly said.
"The regulator would argue that the cost of call termination should be applied according to the principles of non-discrimination and cost orientation," he said.
"A country should be free to set its own call termination charges within the constraints of cost orientation and within the constraints of competition," he said.
Once effective competition was established, the regulator's role would be phased out, Kelly said.
